Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:20: And what he said above, "seeks You early, to cleave to You with abundant love," may be understood through what Rashbi explains (Zohar, Beshalach 46a): that those who stand with the Shechinah at night until the light of morning - at the light of morning, the Holy One, blessed be He, stretches over the Shechinah and over those who partnered with her a thread of Chesed, so that in the morning they cleave to the King with Ahavah Rabbah [Great Love], which is Chesed - and then their desire for love grows greater, for until now they cleaved with a small light, which is the nefesh and is a "lesser love," and in the morning they cleave with Ahavah Rabbah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:21: And it says "until morning breaks" - this is the darkness before dawn, as explained there in Parashat Beshalach. And one must occupy himself with Torah until the light of day, in order to bind the attribute of night to day - and this is the nature of the word "until." And the word "breaks" is precise with the word "seeks early" [ashacharecha], which is a term related to "shachar" [dawn] and not "boker" [morning] - for the beginning of morning is the dawn, and then the light of Chesed begins to be aroused, and then they receive gifts from the King. And in these words there: when night departs and morning comes, and it darkens and grows dim, then the King [comes] to the Matronita in the secret of joy, and gives her gifts, and to all the members of His Heichal - happy is the portion of one who is among the count - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:22: Behold, this is explained from the discourse, and from within it the secret of love is explained as we have explained it. And although he made it dependent specifically on the night, and it would be fitting that this love be constant in a person, and that the Holy One, blessed be He, be his soul and spirit forever, from the intensity of love - rather, the matter is that the reality of the lover's desire already preceded him during the day of love, but at night the love grows stronger in him, and he says in his heart, when will the night come, that I may arise to perform my Creator's will and complete what I owe from love of Him, blessed be He? And with this the language of Rashbi, peace be upon him, is precise, that he took the word "at night," "a person must," and did not take the whole language of the verse, "my soul desires You in the night" - for the matter of "desires You" applies even by day, but at night is when he needs the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the love already preceded him by day. And he divided the verse with a sharp knife, into three clauses: the first, "my soul"; the second, "desires You"; the third, "in the night" - and so the cantillation marks prove this: on the word "nafshi" [my soul], a reversed shofar; "avitecha" [desires You], two staffs; "balailah" [in the night], a small zakef.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:23: Further, it is possible that the reason love is made dependent on rising at midnight to occupy oneself with Torah is that there is no greater love for the Holy One, blessed be He, than this - for one nullifies the desire of the body, which loves sleep and pleasure, because of love of one's Creator, which is itself the love of one's soul, as we explained; and although he suffers, he bears the suffering for the sake of love of his Creator - and this is similar to what the verse says (Song of Songs 1:13), "a bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, lodging between my breasts," which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Shabbat 88b): although he embitters and angers me, he lodges between my breasts - and he thereby fulfills the commandment, "and you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart" (Deuteronomy 6:5) - with both your inclinations, the good inclination and the evil inclination (Berachot 9:5).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:24: And concerning the evil inclination, they explain in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (page 163a), that the subduing of the inclination is complete love - that the inclination is subdued beneath the good inclination for the sake of love of the Creator. And for this reason they say in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (13a), that one who rises at midnight is called "a servant of the LORD," explaining the psalm (Psalms 134:1), "behold, bless the LORD, all you servants of the LORD," as referring to those who rise in the middle of the night; and it is fitting that he be called "a servant of the LORD," because one who subdues his inclination against the desires of his body and suffers for the sake of love of his Creator is called "a servant of the LORD," for he serves the LORD and not his body - but one who does not rise, wishing to sleep to give his body rest, is a servant of his inclination and his body, and not a servant of his soul and his Creator.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:25: And this is a general principle for all service dependent on love: that at the time a person subdues his inclination and suffers for the sake of the service of the LORD, he is called a lover of the Name and is not called a lover of his own inclination; and if he does not subdue his inclination, he is called a servant of his inclination. It follows that love is the key to the fulfillment of the entire Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:26: Further, a person acquires the attribute of love by rising at midnight, considering the great kindness the Creator did for him in returning his soul to his body and reviving him from sleep, which is one-sixtieth of death; and if a person were to imagine that he had been dead for one day - as happened to Rabbi Yosi of Pekiin, mentioned in the Zohar, Parashat Balak (204b) - how much love would he owe the Creator, who did such good for him! And by this analogy - that at night a person sleeps, and sleep is one-sixtieth of death, and how many sleep in their beds and do not rise - when he awakens from his sleep, he should kindle his soul in love of the Creator, who returned his soul to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:27: And for this they instituted the praise, "my God, the soul You gave me is pure" - and this "my God" refers to the One who watches over me and to whom I am cleaved; and in the way of the secret, it is the Shechinah, with whom the soul was in deposit, as it says, "into Your hand I entrust my spirit." And since, while he was asleep, he was separated from the cleaving of love, when sleep, which is [a form of] death, ruled over the body, upon the return of the soul and his being alive, behold, he is cleaved to Him, blessed be He - and therefore, "as long as the soul is within me, I give thanks before You, O LORD, my God." And it would be fitting that with every breath we take, we be cleaved to Him, blessed be He - and this is "as long as the soul is within me," because He stands over our heads - and this is "I give thanks before You" - and this is the Shechinah above one's head, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (see Kiddushin 31a, Kohelet Rabbah 9:8), flowing life to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:28: And when he awakens from his sleep, he should be aroused in love of the Creator who gave him life, and consider that this is how He is destined to give him life again at the resurrection of the dead - as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in the Midrash on Lamentations (3:8), "they are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness" (Lamentations 3:23) - Rabbi Alexandri said: because You renew us every single morning, we know that Your faithfulness is great for the resurrection of the dead - to this point. And my teacher, peace be upon him, explained that for this reason the Men of the Great Assembly instituted the words "and You are destined to take it from me and restore it within me in the future to come" - meaning that "in the future to come" refers to the resurrection of the dead.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:29: Further, our holy Torah explained to us the way to acquire love, how it should be, when it says (Deuteronomy 6:5), "and you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might" - these are three things, and when the three of them are bound together as one in a person, love will be fixed and bound with the LORD within him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:30: And the explanation of these three things is explained in the words of Rashbi (Zohar, Parashat Terumah, page 162b): Rabbi Yitzchak was often found before Rabbi Elazar. He said to him: certainly, the love a person has for the Holy One, blessed be He, is aroused only from the heart, for the heart is the arousal to arouse love toward Him, and the Merciful One requires the heart. If so, why is it written "with all your heart" and afterward "with all your soul" - implying that there are two aspects, one the heart and one the soul? If the heart is the essential thing, what need is there for the soul?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:31: He said to him: certainly, the heart and the soul are two, and they unite into one - for the heart, the soul, and the wealth are all united with one another, and the heart is the foundation of everything. And it has already been established that "with all your heart" [bechol levavcha, with a doubled letter bet implying "two hearts"] refers to the two inclinations, the good inclination and the evil inclination, and these two, each and every one, is called "lev" [heart] - this one is called "a pure heart" and this one is called "an evil heart," and therefore it is "levavcha," referring to the good inclination and the evil inclination. "And with all your soul" - it should have said "and your soul"; what is "and with all your soul"? Why does it say "and with all"? Rather, to include nefesh, ruach, and neshamah - this is "and with all your soul": everything this "nefesh" grasps. "And with all your might" - likewise, however many kinds of wealth there are. And therefore, all these differ from one another, and it says "with all," [meaning] the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, is that all this be given over, to love Him with each and every one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:32: And should you say, how can one love Him through the evil inclination, for the evil inclination is an accuser, that a person not approach the service of the Holy One, blessed be He - how can he love Him through it? This is an even greater service of the Holy One, blessed be He, when this evil inclination is subdued because of the love with which he loves the Holy One, blessed be He - for when this evil inclination is subdued and that person breaks it, this is the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, because he knew how to bring that evil inclination near to the service of the Holy One, blessed be He - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:33: And Rashbi explains (Zohar, Parashat Va'etchanan, page 267a), "and with all your might," well explained: "and with all your might" - why? Whether money falls to him through inheritance or from another source, since it is his spirit [i.e., considered as precious to him as his spirit], therefore it is written "with all your might [me'odecha]" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:34: And what emerges for us from the general sense of the discourse, for this exposition of love, is: two things constitute the essence of love, namely "with all your heart" and "with all your soul," and the third, "with all your might," is a consequence that results from love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:35: "With all your heart" - meaning, with both your inclinations, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in the Mishnah (Berachot 9:5); and the intent is that he should subdue the evil inclination for the sake of love of his Creator, and thereby attain love - as the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot writes (Gate of Self-Reckoning, chapter 7, reckoning 24), that one must remove love of this world from his heart and strengthen love of the World to Come - as one of the sages said, just as water and fire cannot be combined in one vessel, so love of this world and love of the World to Come cannot be combined in the heart of the believer. And he wrote in the Gate of Love (Introduction) that it is impossible for a person to attain the level of love of the [divine] Name, which is cleaving, the great virtue above which there is none, unless the fear of the LORD - which is abstinence from the desires of this world - precedes it. And his words are the words of the living God, for so in the discourse (Sotah 49a) of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, which we shall explain, he says: piety [chasidut] is greater than all of them - and piety is love, as we shall explain; and before piety comes watchfulness, and alacrity, and so on. It follows that to attain love of the Creator is to subdue the inclination in all the particulars that will be explained, with God's help - and this is "with all your heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:36: Indeed, we must be precise as to why "with all" [bechol] is added, since "your heart" [levavcha] already implies two, the good inclination and the evil inclination. And it is possible [to explain] through what is explained (Zohar, Parashat Va'era, 27a), in these words: "with all your heart" - this is the right and the left, called the good inclination and the evil inclination - to this point. And the intent is that from the right and left, the good inclination and the evil inclination are drawn down below, and there it is explained in the way of unification and pairing; indeed, what pertains to our subject is what is explained above this, on the verse (Deuteronomy 4:39), "and you shall consider in your heart that the LORD, He is God" - and we explained that discourse in the Gate of Fear, chapter 4 - that when a person subdues the evil inclination, he also thereby causes the left above to be included beneath the right, which is the essence of love, as we explained in chapter 1. And therefore the extra word "with all" in "with all your heart" is to include the supernal roots from which the good inclination and the evil inclination are drawn, so that the left always be included in the right, and the right, which is love, prevail.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:37: "And with all your soul" - they explain that this is to include nefesh, ruach, and neshamah. We must understand what the matter of love has to do with nefesh, ruach, and neshamah - for until now we have not heard of distinctions in the reality of love, and it is simple that one must love with all three, if he has merited them; and if he has not merited all three, he should love with what he has.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:38: And it appears to me, in explaining this matter, through what we explained - that the matter of the word "ahavah" [love] is the bond and cleaving of a person's soul to the Emanator and His attributes - and the intent is that "you shall love the LORD with all your soul" means that you shall cleave to Him with all the parts within you: the intent being to cleave the portion of the nefesh within him to the portion of the supernal nefesh, from the place from which the nefesh is flowed to him; and likewise to cleave the portion of the ruach within him to the portion of the supernal ruach whose form remains above - as we wrote in the Gate of Fear, chapter 9, that as the soul passes, its form remains there, as Rashbi explains (Vayechi 244a) in the discourse "set me as a seal"; see there. And likewise to cleave the portion of the neshamah within him to the portion of the form of the place of the supernal neshamah. And these three realities are within Atzilut: nefesh, ruach, neshamah of Atzilut; and there is nefesh, ruach, neshamah of the level of Ofan, Chayah, Kisei [Throne], as explained in the Tikkunim (23a); see there. And the reality of the completeness of love is that all three be bound, each person according to his own aspect: if he has merited the lower nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, he cleaves to all three at their source according to his aspect; and if he has merited the nefesh, ruach, and neshamah of Atzilut, he binds them according to his merit. And the essence of the command "with all your soul" is that he strive to attain everything that this "soul" holds, so that your love be complete in all the worlds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:39: And know that just as there is, in the reality of love, the secret of kisses, as we explained in the previous chapter, so too in every single world - Ofan, Chayah, and Kisei - there are kisses within them. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Song of Songs [passage] (Zohar Chadash 63b), in these words: at the time the Cherubim spread their wings from below, letters fly from below to above and letters from above to below, and these enter into those and are included one within the other in a kiss of love; once the letters join, all the levels, lower and upper, and all the worlds join together as one and kiss one another in a kiss of love, until they all become one, and the Holy One, blessed be He, one, without any separation at all. All kisses of love are only to become one totality, to be included one within the other without separation, and therefore these kisses are, in everything, to become one totality within one totality - letters within letters, worlds within worlds, levels within levels, a woman with her husband, that all become one - to this point. Behold, it is explicit that the reality of kisses exists in all the worlds - the reality of kisses being that the caused things bind to one another and are included one within the other, from the side of their inner essence and from the side of their externality, which are the vessels. If so, it emerges for us that it is possible for a person to have love in the [divine] Name from the side of the nefesh, and cleave to YHVH, which is the love we explained in chapter 2 - for in every single world, YHVH is found, as we explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 1, and the Cause of all causes shines within them all; and each person, according to what he has merited, cleaves in that portion he has merited, and there the Creator is found with him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:40: Indeed, we do not deny that the love of one who has a neshamah is not equal to that of one who has a ruach, nor to that of one who has only a nefesh - for according to his ascent up the rungs of the ladder, so his soul and body are refined, and love becomes constant, such that he cannot be separated from the Creator out of his abundant desire for Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:41: And the reason is that the nefesh, which is of the level of Sandalfon within Asiyah, is close to the husks, and the husks are a screen separating between his soul and his God, and therefore his love for the Blessed Name will not remain constant, except for a very brief time. And when he merits the ruach of Metatron, which is already more separated from the husks, love will remain more constant in him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:42: And when he merits the neshamah, which is from the Throne, where there is no husk at all - for it is the King's garment on Sabbaths and festivals - then his love will be cleaved to the [divine] Name always, and he will disdain the governance of the body from this world, which is governed through the six weekdays, and he will strip away love of this world, since this world is clothed in the serpent's skin, and clothe himself with love of the world of souls, where the souls are bound up in the bundle of life, cleaved to their Creator, and he will cleave to what is destined to be in the end and in its ultimate future - "for who is wise? One who foresees what is born [i.e., the consequences]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:43: As the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot writes (Gate of Self-Reckoning, chapter 7), in distancing love of this world - that a person in this world is like a stranger who has arrived in a foreign land, with no one to have pity on him, except that the lord of that country had pity on him as a stranger and taught him the way to arrange his affairs there, and told him that his residence in that land is not permanent, but that he should prepare provisions to go to another, better land - for that person is obligated to prepare provisions and the other conditions of being a stranger, as he, of blessed memory, wrote. And he wrote: and the proof of your being a stranger and alone in this world is that at the time you came forth into existence, and were formed in your mother's womb, if all the people of the world strove to bring you forth a moment earlier, or delay you a moment later, they could not; and so no person has the ability to bring food to you without the help of God, nor to add to your body nor diminish from it. And if you were to consider that the whole world remained for you alone, without any inhabitants, your sustenance reaching you toward your end would not increase by the measure of a mustard seed; and likewise, if [the world's inhabitants] were doubled, your sustenance decreed for you would not decrease by less than a mustard seed, nor more. And likewise, not one of the creatures can benefit you or harm you, nor can any of them add to the days of your life or diminish them; and so too your traits, your nature, and your good and evil deeds. If so, what relationship is there between you and the creatures, or in what closeness are you close to them, or they to you? And you are in this world like a prisoner, whom the majority of its people cannot benefit, nor can the minority harm; and you see in it nothing but a solitary individual who has no companion but his Master, and none has pity on him but his Creator. Therefore, my brother, devote yourself singly to His service, just as He devoted Himself singly to your creation, your governance, your sustenance, your life, and your death; and set His Torah and His support before your eyes, and accept the conditions of strangerhood, which I have aroused you to, upon your soul all your days in this world - and you will attain the pleasantness of the World to Come - to this point. And I have abbreviated some of his words that are not needed for our purpose. It follows that when a person considers his strangerhood in this world, he will strip love of this world from his heart and consider his cleaving to the world of souls, where he is always cleaved to YHVH.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:44: And included in the root of acquiring love is the love of solitude - for while a person desires the company of people, it is impossible for him to be cleaved [to God]. And Rabbi Yitzchak of Acre, peace be upon him, wrote, in these words: one who withdraws into solitude, wishing to merit the virtue of solitude so that peace rest upon him in his lifetime, must bind himself to these three things and distance himself from their opposites, and then peace will rest upon him in his lifetime, and all the more so afterward; and these are: that he be content with his portion, that he love solitude, and that he flee from authority and honor, which is the subduing of the heart. And their opposites: that he not be satisfied with what he has, and not be sated with wealth - "one who loves money is never sated with money" - and that his soul be impatient sitting alone, but in the company of people and their conversation he desires, and rejoices to speak and hear idle words, and that he pursue honor and authority. May the Merciful One grant us merit to bind ourselves to the first three things and to those who possess them, and distance us from the three opposite things and from those who possess them - to this point. And concerning the matter of humility we will elaborate on the matter of distancing from honor.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:45: And let us return to the exposition we were engaged in - that certainly one does not attain the level of cleaving, to be always cleaved in love, except one who has merited the neshamah, where there is no separating screen between him and his God - and this on condition that the subduing of the inclination precede it, as we shall elaborate, with God's help. And therefore we were warned, "and you shall love with all your soul" - "everything this nefesh holds" - so that love be complete in YHVH, and the worlds be included and bind to one another until they become an established throne in which the light of the Emanator shines. And if the worlds do not bind together to become one throne, unified in the ultimate unity, because of blemish, they will not be prepared to receive the light of the Infinite - for such is the way of unity: either it rests entirely as one, or it does not rest at all. And the reason is that all the worlds are as one - this one a throne for that one, and this one for that one, ascending higher and higher, and they are all one stature [komah] - and when there is a blemish in one limb, it is a blemish in the whole.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:46: And the blemish similar to this is the matter of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah - the nefesh is a throne and garment for the ruach, and the ruach is a throne and garment for the neshamah. Behold, when there is a blemish in the nefesh, the ruach and neshamah depart from over the nefesh, for "whoever has a blemish shall not approach"; and the flow departs from over the ruach, because it has no vessel through which to flow; and so it departs from over the neshamah, because it does not flow to the ruach - and in this manner the flow departs, higher and higher. And this is what they said (Yoma 39a): a person who defiles himself a little is defiled much more - for when the light departs because of that blemish, impurity increases because of the departure of holiness, as we explained. And likewise concerning the matter of holiness: when a person arouses a small amount of holiness, since all the levels are bound to one another, he is sanctified much more - and all this according to the aspect of the channel of that soul in the Chariot; from its own side it departs, and no person can fix what is crooked except he himself. And my teacher, peace be upon him, brought a pleasant parable along these lines in his book (Pardes Rimonim), in the Gate of Intention.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:47: It follows that the way for a person to cleave to his Creator is through binding nefesh, ruach, and neshamah to their source, and then all the worlds bind together as one through his nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, and he causes the illumination of the Emanator, King of kings of kings, in all the worlds; and this is the secret of kisses in all the worlds, that they bind together and are included one within the other, and likewise his nefesh, ruach, and neshamah shine and are included above and nurse abundant flow from the source of all blessings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:48: And there is proof for us, from the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, that cleaving comes through nefesh, ruach, and neshamah; in these words, in Bereshit Rabbah (80:7): Rabbi Shimon ben Lavi said, in three terms of affection did the Holy One, blessed be He, hold Israel dear: in cleaving [devikah], in desire [chashikah], and in delight [chafitzah]. In cleaving, from where? As it is said (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to the LORD your God." In desire, from where? As it is said (ibid. 7:7), "the LORD desired you." In delight, from where? As it is said (Malachi 3:12), "and all the nations shall call you happy, for you shall be a delightful land." And we learn [these terms] from the passage concerning that wicked man [Shechem]: in cleaving (Genesis 34:3), "and his soul cleaved to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob"; in desire, it is written (ibid. 34:8), "the soul of my son Shechem desires your daughter"; in delight (ibid. 34:19), "for he delighted in Jacob's daughter."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:49: Rabbi Abba ben Elisha adds two more: in love and in speech. In love (Malachi 1:2), "I have loved you, says the LORD." In speech (Isaiah 40:2), "speak to the heart of Jerusalem." And we learn [these] from the passage concerning that wicked man: in love (Genesis 34:3), "and he loved the young woman"; in speech (ibid.), "and he spoke to the heart of the young woman" - words that comfort the heart - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:50: It is fitting to raise one point: why did Rabbi Shimon ben Lavi count only three, since we find five in the passage concerning that wicked man, as Rabbi Abba ben Elisha said? Rather, the matter is that Rabbi Shimon ben Lavi wished to count only the three that are essential, corresponding to nefesh, ruach, and neshamah. And Rabbi Abba ben Elisha, who counted five, did so because we find that the soul has five names, as Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains (Zohar, Terumah 158b): "and you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart" - this is the body; "and with all your soul" - this is the soul, which has five names: neshamah, nefesh, ruach, chayah, yechidah. "And with all your might" - with all your wealth. The Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah will not depart from you through all of these - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:51: And let us return to the particulars of the discourse: that the Holy One, blessed be He, held Israel dear in three terms of affection, because the flow of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah to us comes from Him, blessed be He, and through these precious portions we have from Him, blessed be He, He is adorned within us - and He flowed these portions into us only out of His great affection for us, along the lines of (Deuteronomy 10:15), "only in your fathers did the LORD delight [chashak], to love them" - which Rashbi explains (Zohar, Va'etchanan 262b) as meaning that He made them a supernal Chariot; in these words: it is taught, Rabbi Abba [said], "only in your fathers did the LORD delight," and so on - from here Rabbi Shimon said, the fathers are the supernal, holy Chariot - and it is written "the LORD delighted"; and he says afterward, "only in your fathers" is three, and the Chariot is four - and from where do we derive the fourth? As it is written, "and He chose their seed after them" - what does this imply? To include David the king among them, as the fourth to complete the holy Chariot - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:52: And what he said, "and it is written, the LORD delighted [chashak]" - the intent is as it is written in the Tikkunim (page 20b), that the Name YHVH is vocalized with sheva, cholam, kamatz - kamatz in Chesed, sheva in Gevurah, cholam in Tiferet, and the mnemonic for these three vowel-points is "CHaSHaK" [an acronym of the vowels]. And they said, of blessed memory, that at the time [the Name is vocalized] sheva, kamatz, cholam, it is hinted, "for he has desired [chashak] Me, therefore I will deliver him" (Psalms 91:14) - "only in your fathers did He desire [chashak]" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:53: And the fact that the fathers are a Chariot above comes from His abundant love, blessed be He, for us, to flow to them holy souls from above - as Rashbi explains (Zohar, Emor 98b): happy is Israel, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, drew near to Him from among all the nations of the world, and He desired them, and from a distant place He drew them near to Him - this is what is written (Joshua 24:2), "thus says the LORD, your fathers dwelt of old on the other side of the river," and it is written, "and I took your father," and so on, "from the other side of the river." And he raised a difficulty: this matter Israel and Joshua already knew - why does it say "thus says the LORD"? And he answered: rather, certainly, the hidden meaning of the matter is that the Holy One, blessed be He, did great good to Israel in that He desired the fathers and made them a holy Chariot for His glory, and He brought them forth from within the supernal, precious River - to the extent relevant here. For the Holy One, blessed be He, did a great kindness for Israel in bringing forth the root of souls from the highest above, and no [prior] deed or arousal on the part of the fathers preceded the Holy One, blessed be He's emanating their souls from beyond the river - this is the nature of the word "chashak" [the LORD desired] - that the desire and arousal of love began with Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:54: And these are the three terms of affection with which the Holy One, blessed be He, held Israel dear, corresponding to nefesh, ruach, neshamah, which He flowed into us out of His abundant affection. Corresponding to the aspect of the nefesh, he says "in cleaving," as it is said, "but you who cleave to the LORD your God, [are all] alive" - and Rashbi explains that Israel cleave to the secret of the blue [techelet] fire within the Shechinah, giving her the arousal of their good deeds, and even though this blue is [an aspect of] consumption, destruction, and judgment, nevertheless we are alive. In these words (Zohar, Bereshit 51a): come and see, there is no arousal to kindle this blue light, to unite with the white light, except through Israel, who cleave beneath it. And come and see: although the way of this blue light is dark, to destroy everything that cleaves to it beneath it, Israel cleave to it, beneath it, and yet endure - this is what is written, "but you who cleave to the LORD your God" - and not "our God," but rather "the LORD your God" - to that black blue that consumes and destroys everything cleaved beneath it, yet you cleave to it and endure, as it is written, "all of you alive today" - to this point. Behold, it is explained from this discourse that this entire verse is spoken concerning the aspect of the Shechinah, in the aspect of the blue fire within her - and this corresponds to the aspect of the nefesh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:55: And with the introduction of the discourse we copied from the book of the Zohar, one doubt found in the discourse is resolved: how does it bring proof from the verse "but you who cleave" for the term of affection that the Holy One, blessed be He, held Israel dear, when in the other verses brought, the affection of the Holy One, blessed be He, [for Israel] is clear - "only in your fathers did the LORD delight" - whereas this verse concerns Israel, that when they are cleaved to the LORD they are alive, and it does not indicate the cleaving of the Holy One, blessed be He, to them? Indeed, from what we wrote at the beginning of the discourse - "there is no arousal to kindle this blue light... except through Israel" - it follows that the explanation of "but you who cleave to the LORD" must also teach that the word "who cleave" refers back also to "your God" [Elohechem] - that He is cleaved to you as well as you are cleaved to Him, because it [the blue light] requires the arousal of your deeds to unite with the white light - and this is "Elohechem," in the possessive referring to you, as Rashbi explains, that He is cleaved to you.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:56: Further, it is possible to say that the discourse's proof of the term of affection comes from a superfluous word in the verse, which is "YHVH" - for it should properly have said "but you who cleave to your God" [Eloheichem], and from its saying "in the LORD" [ba-Shem], it indicates the LORD's cleaving to them. And this is because the souls of Israel are from the side of the male, as explained in Parashat Vayechi (245a), concerning a difficulty Rashbi, peace be upon him, raised about the fact that we find the female pursuing the male, which is not to the credit of the female - and he answered that since the branches of the male are the ones aroused, it follows that the male is the one who arouses, for Tiferet flows its flow into its branches - it follows that YHVH, who is Tiferet, is also cleaved to them, so that He be the one who arouses.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:57: And in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Kedoshim 5) it says that this is by a gezeirah shavah [verbal analogy], in these words: (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I the LORD am holy" - this is what Scripture says, "but you who cleave to the LORD," and it is written (Jeremiah 13:11), "for as the belt cleaves to the loins of a man, so have I made cleave to Me," and so on. It follows that just as the verse "as the belt cleaves," and so on, "so have I made cleave," refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, making them cleave to Himself, so too the verse "but you who cleave" [means the same]. And this discourse is also brought at length in the Yalkut on Jeremiah, in explaining the verse "as the belt cleaves" - and we will copy the whole discourse below, in [discussing] the virtue of cleaving.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:58: Corresponding to the aspect of the ruach, he says "in desire," as it is written, "the LORD desired you" - and we have already explained that this is said of the three Patriarchs, and Tiferet, in which the Name YHVH is vocalized sheva, cholam, kamatz, indicating that it is included of all three [Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet] - and this corresponds to the ruach, which is from it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:59: Corresponding to the neshamah, he says "in delight," as it is written, "and all the nations shall call you happy," and so on, "for you shall be a delightful land." And there is proof in the verse in three ways that this is said corresponding to the neshamah, which is from the side of Imma. The first, the word "ve'ishru" [shall call happy], which is explained in the Zohar (Vayechi 246a), on (Genesis 49:20), "out of Asher his bread shall be fat" - that "Asher" is the World to Come. The second, "for you shall be" [ki tihyu atem] - and they explain (Zohar, Bo 43b), on the verse "sanctify to Me," that the word "to Me" [li] refers to Binah; see there. The third, "a delightful land [eretz cheifetz]" - meaning a land that nurses from the [supernal] will [ratzon], which is cleaved to Keter [via] Chochmah - and this is the supernal Land, also called the Land of the Living.
